# Define an application-wide Content Security Policy.
# https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Headers/Content-Security-Policy
#
# Directives are configurable via environment variables with fallback to config.x
# settings. This allows fizzy-saas (or other deployments) to extend the base policy
# without duplicating it.
#
# ENV vars (space-separated sources):
#   CSP_DEFAULT_SRC, CSP_SCRIPT_SRC, CSP_STYLE_SRC, CSP_CONNECT_SRC, CSP_FRAME_SRC,
#   CSP_IMG_SRC, CSP_FONT_SRC, CSP_MEDIA_SRC, CSP_WORKER_SRC, CSP_FRAME_ANCESTORS,
#   CSP_FORM_ACTION, CSP_REPORT_URI, CSP_REPORT_ONLY, DISABLE_CSP
#
# config.x.content_security_policy.* (string, space-separated string, or array):
#   script_src, style_src, connect_src, frame_src, img_src, font_src, media_src,
#   worker_src, frame_ancestors, form_action, report_uri, report_only

Rails.application.configure do
  # Helper to get additional CSP sources from ENV or config.x.
  # Supports: nil, string, space-separated string, or array.
  sources = ->(directive) do
    env_key = "CSP_#{directive.to_s.upcase}"
    value = if ENV.key?(env_key)
      ENV[env_key]
    else
      config.x.content_security_policy.send(directive)
    end

    case value
    when nil then []
    when Array then value
    when String then value.split
    else []
    end
  end

  # Report URI and report-only mode
  report_uri = ENV.fetch("CSP_REPORT_URI") { config.x.content_security_policy.report_uri }
  report_only =
    if ENV.key?("CSP_REPORT_ONLY")
      ENV["CSP_REPORT_ONLY"] == "true"
    else
      config.x.content_security_policy.report_only
    end

  # Generate nonces for importmap and inline scripts
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_generator = ->(request) { SecureRandom.base64(16) }
  config.content_security_policy_nonce_directives = %w[ script-src ]

  config.content_security_policy do |policy|
    policy.default_src :self, *sources.(:default_src)
    policy.script_src :self, *sources.(:script_src)
    policy.connect_src :self, *sources.(:connect_src)
    policy.frame_src :self, *sources.(:frame_src)

    # Don't fight user tools: permit inline styles, data:/https: sources, and
    # blob: workers for accessibility extensions, privacy tools, and custom fonts.
    policy.style_src :self, :unsafe_inline, *sources.(:style_src)
    policy.img_src :self, "blob:", "data:", "https:", *sources.(:img_src)
    policy.font_src :self, "data:", "https:", *sources.(:font_src)
    policy.media_src :self, "blob:", "data:", "https:", *sources.(:media_src)
    policy.worker_src :self, "blob:", *sources.(:worker_src)

    # Security-critical defaults (not configurable)
    policy.object_src :none
    policy.base_uri :none

    policy.form_action :self, *sources.(:form_action)
    policy.frame_ancestors :self, *sources.(:frame_ancestors)

    # Specify URI for violation reports (e.g., Sentry CSP endpoint)
    policy.report_uri report_uri if report_uri
  end

  # Report violations without enforcing the policy.
  config.content_security_policy_report_only = report_only
end unless ENV["DISABLE_CSP"]

#   identifier. Defaults to +ActionPack::WebAuthn::Current.host+.
#
# [+name+]

#   during ceremonies. Defaults to +Rails.application.name+.
class ActionPack::WebAuthn::RelyingParty

  # Unlike dotenv, this regex does not match escaped
  # parentheses when looking for command substitutions.
  INTERPOLATED_SHELL_COMMAND = /
    (?<backslash>\\)?          # is it escaped with a backslash?
    \$                         # literal $
    (?<cmd>                    # collect command content for eval
      \(                       # require opening paren
      (?:\\.|[^()\\]|\g<cmd>)+ # allow any number of non-parens or escaped
                               # parens (by nesting the <cmd> expression
                               # recursively)
      \)                       # require closing paren
    )
  /x

  class << self
    def install!
      ::Dotenv::Parser.substitutions.map! { |sub| sub == ::Dotenv::Substitutions::Command ? self : sub }
    end

    def call(value, env, overwrite: false)
      # Process interpolated shell commands
      value.gsub(INTERPOLATED_SHELL_COMMAND) do |*|
        # Eliminate opening and closing parentheses
        command = $LAST_MATCH_INFO[:cmd][1..-2]

        if $LAST_MATCH_INFO[:backslash]
          # Command is escaped, don't replace it.
          $LAST_MATCH_INFO[0][1..]
        else
          command = ::Dotenv::Substitutions::Variable.call(command, env)
          if command =~ /\A\s*kamal\s*secrets\s+/
            # Inline the command
            inline_secrets_command(command)
          else
            # Execute the command and return the value
            `#{command}`.chomp
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def inline_secrets_command(command)
      Kamal::Cli::Main.start(command.shellsplit[1..] + [ "--inline" ]).chomp
    end
  end
end
"

module Kamal::Cli
  class Base < Thor
    include SSHKit::DSL

    VERBOSITY = { verbose: :debug, quiet: :error }.freeze

    def self.exit_on_failure?() true end
    def self.dynamic_command_class() Kamal::Cli::Alias::Command end

    class_option :verbose, type: :boolean, aliases: "-v", desc: "Detailed logging"
    class_option :quiet, type: :boolean, aliases: "-q", desc: "Minimal logging"

    class_option :hosts, aliases: "-h", desc: "Run commands on these hosts instead of all (separate by comma, supports wildcards with *)"
    class_option :roles, aliases: "-r", desc: "Run commands on these roles instead of all (separate by comma, supports wildcards with *)"

    class_option :destination, aliases: "-d", desc: "Specify destination to be used for config file (staging -> deploy.staging.yml)"

            commander.verbosity = VERBOSITY[:verbose]
          end

      end

        started_at = Time.now
        yield
        Time.now - started_at
      ensure
        runtime = Time.now - started_at
        puts "  Finished all in #{sprintf("%.1f seconds", runtime)}"
      end

      def with_lock
        if KAMAL.holding_lock?
          yield
        else
          acquire_lock

          begin
            yield
          rescue
            begin
              release_lock
            rescue => e
              say "Error releasing the deploy lock: #{e.message}", :red
            end
            raise
          end

          release_lock
        end
      end

class Kamal::Cli::Secrets < Kamal::Cli::Base
  desc "fetch [SECRETS...]", "Fetch secrets from a vault"
  option :adapter, type: :string, aliases: "-a", required: true, desc: "Which vault adapter to use"
  option :account, type: :string, required: false, desc: "The account identifier or username"
  option :from, type: :string, required: false, desc: "A vault or folder to fetch the secrets from"
  option :inline, type: :boolean, required: false, hidden: true
  def fetch(*secrets)
    adapter = initialize_adapter(options[:adapter])

    if adapter.requires_account? && options[:account].blank?
      return puts "No value provided for required options '--account'"
    end

    results = adapter.fetch(secrets, **options.slice(:account, :from).symbolize_keys)
    json = JSON.dump(results)

    return_or_puts options[:inline] ? json.shellescape : json, inline: options[:inline]
  end

  desc "extract", "Extract a single secret from the results of a fetch call"
  option :inline, type: :boolean, required: false, hidden: true
  def extract(name, secrets)
    parsed_secrets = JSON.parse(secrets)
    value = parsed_secrets[name] || parsed_secrets.find { |k, v| k.end_with?("/#{name}") }&.last

    raise "Could not find secret #{name}" if value.nil?

    return_or_puts value, inline: options[:inline]
  end

  desc "print", "Print the secrets (for debugging)"
  def print
    KAMAL.config.secrets.to_h.each do |key, value|
      puts "#{key}=#{value}"
    end
  end

  private
    def initialize_adapter(adapter)
      Kamal::Secrets::Adapters.lookup(adapter)
    end

    def return_or_puts(value, inline: nil)
      if inline
        value
      else
        puts value
      end
    end
end
"
}

#!/bin/sh
# Keep the developer's own PATH -- bin/setup accepts whichever mise it finds and
# upgrades that one -- but drop relative entries first. Shipyard puts ./bin at
# high precedence, and a hook runs with a checkout as its cwd, so a relative
# entry resolves against whatever tree you happen to be committing in.
#
# That is all this prevents: accidental shadowing. It is deliberately not a
# defence against a hostile checkout, because there cannot be one here. Git runs
# THIS file, which the repository tracks under core.hooksPath, and shipyard
# trusts .mise.toml under the worktree roots -- so a checkout already decides
# what executes long before any PATH is examined. Earlier revisions filtered
# absolute in-tree paths too, canonicalising against the worktree; that defended
# a boundary that does not exist, and cost three rounds of its own bugs.
#
# Filtered with shell builtins so the filter itself does not come from the PATH
# being filtered.
absolute=''
IFS=:
for dir in $PATH; do
  case $dir in /*) absolute="${absolute:+$absolute:}$dir" ;; esac
done
unset IFS

# Then mise's standard install locations, for GUI clients: they run no login
# profile, so their PATH is whatever launchd or systemd provides.
#
# Retiring bin/bcenv, which re-execed through a login shell, gives up what that
# profile provided. Two consequences, both confined to GUI launches. A mise
# reachable only through the profile is not found -- that one is accepted, and
# the diagnostic below says so. And shipyard's PATH ordering does not apply, so
# where bin/setup left an older package-manager mise beside a newer mise.run
# one, position no longer favours the newer. That second one is not accepted:
# it is why the selection below goes by version floor rather than PATH order.
#
# A third is accepted. If the login profile sets MISE_DATA_DIR or XDG_DATA_HOME,
# bin/setup installed the toolchain into that store, and a GUI launch -- having
# no profile -- points mise at its default one instead. mise provisions the
# project's toolchain there: the right versions, but ~26s the first time and
# again after each version bump. bin/bcenv covered this by sourcing a profile;
# this does not. Accepted rather than fixed, because the alternative is state
# bin/setup must write and this hook must keep in step, across five
# repositories, for a configuration shipyard does not create.
#
# Do not "fix" it by turning auto-install off. MISE_AUTO_INSTALL=0 returns in
# 0s with /usr/bin/ruby 2.6.10 instead of the project's 3.4.10 -- silently the
# wrong toolchain, which is the single outcome this hook exists to prevent. The
# delay is mise doing the right thing.
PATH="${absolute:+$absolute:}$HOME/.local/bin:/opt/homebrew/bin:/usr/local/bin:/usr/bin:/bin"
export PATH

# Several mise installations can coexist: bin/setup upgrades whichever one it
# resolved and leaves the rest in place, so a stale mise.run copy in
# ~/.local/bin can sit beside a current brew or pacman one, or the reverse. A
# terminal orders them through the login profile; a GUI launch does not, and
# designers here do commit from GUI clients. So pick the first installation
# that satisfies this project's floor rather than the first on PATH.
min_version=$(sed -n 's/^[[:space:]]*min_version[[:space:]]*=[[:space:]]*"\([^"]*\)".*/\1/p' .mise.toml 2>/dev/null | head -1)
mise=''
first_mise=''
IFS=:
for dir in $PATH; do
  [ -x "$dir/mise" ] || continue
  [ -n "$first_mise" ] || first_mise="$dir/mise"
  [ -n "$min_version" ] || { mise="$dir/mise"; break; }
  # MISE_OFFLINE: `mise --version` also checks for a newer mise, which would be
  # a network round trip per candidate on every commit.
  version=$(MISE_OFFLINE=1 "$dir/mise" --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{ print $1; exit }')
  [ -n "$version" ] || continue
  # `sort -V` orders 2026.7.10 ahead of 2026.7.10-rc.1, so compare the release
  # part and never let a prerelease satisfy the stable floor it precedes.
  release=${version%%-*}
  [ "$(printf '%s\n%s\n' "$min_version" "$release" | sort -V | head -1)" = "$min_version" ] || continue
  [ "$release" != "$version" ] && [ "$release" = "$min_version" ] && continue
  mise="$dir/mise"
  break
done
unset IFS

# Nothing satisfied the floor: use the first found and let mise print its own
# version error, which names both versions.
[ -n "$mise" ] || mise=$first_mise

[ -n "$mise" ] || {
  cat >&2 <<EOF
pre-commit: mise not found.

If this succeeds in a terminal but fails from a GUI git client, your mise is
reachable only through your login profile, which GUI clients do not run.
Rerunning bin/setup will not help: it accepts that installation as-is.

Make mise reachable without your profile -- symlink or install it into
~/.local/bin (or /opt/homebrew/bin, /usr/local/bin, /usr/bin), or add its
directory to the PATH GUI processes inherit.

Searched: $PATH
EOF
  exit 1
}

require "test_helper"

class SmtpDeliveryErrorTest < ActionMailer::TestCase
  class TestMailer < ApplicationMailer
    def smtp_syntax_error(message)
      raise Net::SMTPSyntaxError, Net::SMTP::Response.parse(message)
    end

    def smtp_fatal_error(message)
      raise Net::SMTPFatalError, Net::SMTP::Response.parse(message)
    end

    def ephemeral_retry
      self.class.goes_boom_once
    end

    def self.goes_boom_once
      # Stubbed in test to raise exception once
    end
  end
  tests TestMailer

  test "deliver_later ignores bad recipient addresses" do
    assert_nothing_raised do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob do
        TestMailer.smtp_syntax_error("501 5.1.3 Bad recipient address syntax\n").deliver_later
      end
    end
  end

  test "deliver_later ignores rejected recipient addresses" do
    assert_nothing_raised do
      perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob do
        TestMailer.smtp_fatal_error("550 5.1.1 fooaddress: Recipient address rejected: User unknown in local recipient table\n").deliver_later
      end
    end
  end

  test "deliver_later re-raises other SMTP syntax errors" do
    perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob do
      assert_raises Net::SMTPSyntaxError do
        TestMailer.smtp_syntax_error("not a recipient address error").deliver_later
      end
    end
  end


  [ Net::OpenTimeout, Net::ReadTimeout, Net::SMTPServerBusy.new(Net::SMTP::Response.parse("4xx Server Busy")) ].each do |exception|
    test "deliver_later retries temporary #{exception}" do
      TestMailer.stubs(:goes_boom_once).raises(exception).then.returns(nil)

      perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob do
        assert_nothing_raised do
          TestMailer.ephemeral_retry.deliver_later
        end
      end
    end
  end
end

Time to dive into `/usr/local/bundle/gems/kamal-2.11.0/lib/kamal/configuration/env.rb` and see exactly how Kamal handles environment variable precedence when the same key is defined in both clear and secret contexts.   include Kamal::Configuration::Validation

  attr_reader :context, :clear, :secrets, :secret_keys
  delegate :argumentize, to: Kamal::Utils

  def initialize(config:, secrets:, context: "env")
    @clear = config.fetch("clear", config.key?("secret") || config.key?("tags") ? {} : config)
    @secrets = secrets
    @secret_keys = config.fetch("secret", [])

  end

  def secrets_io
    Kamal::EnvFile.new(aliased_secrets).to_io
  end

  def merge(other)
    self.class.new \
      config: { "clear" => clear.merge(other.clear), "secret" => secret_keys | other.secret_keys },
      secrets: secrets

ruby -e '
  path = "config/environments/production.rb"
  content = File.read(path)
  target = "  # Ignore bad email addresses and do not raise email delivery errors.\n  # Set this to true and configure the email server for immediate delivery to raise delivery errors.\n  # config.action_mailer.raise_delivery_errors = false\n"
  addition = <<~RUBY
  #{target.chomp}

    if app_host = ENV["APP_HOST"].presence
      app_host = app_host.sub(%r{\\Ahttps?://}, "").chomp("/")
      protocol = (config.assume_ssl || config.force_ssl) ? "https" : "http"
      url_options = { host: app_host, protocol: protocol }

      routes.default_url_options = url_options
      config.action_controller.default_url_options = url_options
      config.action_mailer.default_url_options = url_options
    end

    if smtp_address = ENV["SMTP_ADDRESS"].presence
      smtp_port = Integer(ENV.fetch("SMTP_PORT", 587))
      smtp_tls = ENV["SMTP_TLS"] == "true" || ENV["SMTP_SSL"] == "true" || (smtp_port == 465 && ENV["SMTP_TLS"] != "false")

      config.action_mailer.smtp_settings = {
        address: smtp_address,
        port: smtp_port,
        domain: ENV["SMTP_DOMAIN"].presence || app_host,
        user_name: ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"].presence,
        password: ENV["SMTP_PASSWORD"].presence,
        authentication: ENV["SMTP_AUTHENTICATION"].presence&.to_sym,
        tls: (true if smtp_tls),
        enable_starttls_auto: (ENV.fetch("SMTP_ENABLE_STARTTLS_AUTO", "true") == "true" unless smtp_tls),
        openssl_verify_mode: ENV["SMTP_OPENSSL_VERIFY_MODE"].presence
      }.compact
    end
  RUBY
  raise "Target not found" unless content.include?(target)
  File.write(path, content.sub(target, addition))
'

cat <<'EOF' > docs/deployment.md
## Deploying Fizzy with Kamal

Fizzy ships with a single-server [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org) configuration in [`config/deploy.yml`](../config/deploy.yml). Everything runs in one container on one Linux box:

- **Web & assets**: Puma fronted by Thruster behind `kamal-proxy` with automatic Let's Encrypt SSL
- **Database, cache, cable, and job queue**: SQLite stored in a persistent Docker volume (`fizzy_storage:/rails/storage`)
- **File uploads & exports**: Active Storage on local disk inside `/rails/storage`
- **Background jobs**: Solid Queue running inside Puma (`SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA=true`)

### Prerequisites

1. A Linux server (`amd64` or `arm64`) with root SSH access and ports `80` and `443` open. (Kamal will install Docker automatically if needed.)
2. A DNS `A` / `AAAA` record pointing your hostname (for example, `fizzy.example.com`) at your server's IP address.
3. An outbound SMTP server so Fizzy can send sign-in codes and notifications.
4. Docker installed locally on the machine you deploy from.

### 1. Configure your hostname and mail server

Edit [`config/deploy.yml`](../config/deploy.yml) and replace the placeholder values with your own:

- **`servers.web`**: Your server's hostname or IP address (e.g. `fizzy.example.com`)
- **`proxy.host`**: Your public hostname (e.g. `fizzy.example.com`)
- **`env.clear.APP_HOST`**: Your public hostname (e.g. `fizzy.example.com`)
- **`env.clear.MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS`**: Sender address for outbound emails (e.g. `Fizzy <noreply@fizzy.example.com>`)
- **`env.clear.SMTP_ADDRESS`** and **`env.clear.SMTP_PORT`**: Your SMTP server host and port
- **`builder.arch`**: Defaults to `amd64`; change to `arm64` if your server uses an ARM CPU

### 2. Configure your secrets

Secrets are read by [`.kamal/secrets`](../.kamal/secrets) from environment variables (or a password manager via `kamal secrets fetch` — never commit raw credentials to git).

Generate `SECRET_KEY_BASE` and VAPID keys (used for browser Web Push notifications):

```sh
bin/rails secret
bin/rails runner 'vapid = WebPush.generate_key; puts "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=#{vapid.public_key}\nVAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=#{vapid.private_key}"'
```

Export your secrets before deploying (or wire `.kamal/secrets` to 1Password, Bitwarden, or LastPass):

```sh
export SECRET_KEY_BASE="..."
export SMTP_USERNAME="..."
export SMTP_PASSWORD="..."
export VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY="..."
export VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY="..."
```

### 3. Deploy

Run initial setup to bootstrap Docker on the server, start `kamal-proxy` with SSL, create the persistent storage volume, prepare the SQLite databases, and boot Fizzy:

```sh
bin/kamal setup
```

Once setup finishes, open `https://your-host` to create your account.

For subsequent deploys (your SQLite databases and uploaded files in `fizzy_storage` persist across deploys):

```sh
bin/kamal deploy
```
EOF

steps.reasoning_content:
**My Immediate Assessment**

Okay, hold on a second! I need to zoom in and thoroughly examine two key aspects of this output. This is critical.

### The First Observation, and It's a Big One:

I *must* scrutinize `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings` closely, specifically comparing the configurations when testing port 587 versus port 465. Line 4 of section 4 in particular is what catches my eye: `action_mailer.smtp_settings: {address: "smtp.example.com", port: 587, domain: "fizzy.example.com", user_name: "myuser", password: "mypass", enable_starttls_auto: true, open_timeout: 5, read_timeout: 5}`. Wait a minute...why are `open_timeout: 5` and `read_timeout: 5` *still* present within `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings`? I have an inkling.

The Rails framework, through `ActionMailer::Railtie`, merges configurations with the default settings: `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings.merge!(config.action_mailer.smtp_settings)`.

This is important! Let's test port 465 right now.

If `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings` already held `enable_starttls_auto: true` in its initial defaults, and Rails used `.merge!` or if `.compact` omitted `:enable_starttls_auto` when `smtp_tls` was `true`, would `ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings` still contain `enable_starttls_auto: true` alongside `tls: true`?!

steps.message: Let's run a full end-to-end simulation covering Kamal config validation, local SMTP server with AUTH, Deploy #1 (`docker-entrypoint` -> `thrust` -> `puma` + `solid_queue`), user signup via magic-link email delivered by Solid Queue over SMTP, creating an account/board/card/attachment, stopping Deploy #1, starting Deploy #2 (`db:prepare` + server), and verifying all data, sessions, search, and uploaded files survive across deploys!
steps.reasoning_content:
**End-to-End Test Plan: Cleaning Up SMTP & Ensuring Data Persistence**

Okay, so looking at that output, it's clear: `enable_starttls_auto` is redundant when using `port: 465` and `tls: true`. Time to clean up the `storage/production*` environment and verify everything with a fresh test run of `Mail::SMTP.new(ActionMailer::Base.smtp_settings).send(:build_smtp_session)`.

Right, let's craft a complete, end-to-end integration test script. The goal is to simulate the whole user journey, from initial deployment to data persistence across deployments. Here's the plan:

First, we simulate a developer setting up their environment. We'll have them configure their hostname (`fizzy.their-host.test`), mail server (e.g., `127.0.0.1:<mock_smtp_port>`, with `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS="Fizzy <login@their-host.test>"`), and all their secrets, filling in the `config/deploy.yml` file. Kamal will validate the filled-in configuration and secrets, and generate the proper container environment, volume mounts, and `kamal-proxy` SSL target config.

Now, we'll run **Deploy #1**: We'll kick off a local mock SMTP server to verify AUTH PLAIN and capture the sent emails. Then, we execute the application with `/rails/bin/docker-entrypoint ./bin/thrust ./bin/rails server` using the *exact* environment variables from Kamal. We'll verify the proxy health check (`GET /up`). Then, we'll simulate a user signing up at `https://fizzy.their-host.test` using HTTPS-terminated proxy headers. Crucially, we'll confirm that Solid Queue executes the `ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob` on the box and delivers the magic link email to the simulated SMTP server with the correct "From" address and links to the correct domain. We'll extract the 6-digit verification code from the captured email. We'll then complete the sign-up process, create a board, and a card, including an uploaded Active Storage file attachment. Finally, we shut down the Deploy #1 container cleanly using `SIGTERM`.

For **Deploy #2**, we start a *fresh* process, pointing at the same `storage` directory and volumes and run the same command, including the `MIGRATE=1 ./bin/rails db:prepare` step, simulating a database migration and a second deployment. The key here is to verify that *everything* persists: the existing session cookie, the account, the user, the board, the card, the FTS5 search index, *and* the uploaded Active Storage file. We'll ensure everything is served correctly at `https://fizzy.their-host.test`.

Let's get this test running! This will give us confidence in our SMTP settings and ensure that data is persisting correctly across deploys.

arguments.command:
rm -rf storage/production* storage/thruster

bundle exec ruby -rkamal -rsocket -rnet/http -rcookiejar -rjson -rwebrick -rweb-push -e '
  # 1. Start a local mock SMTP server supporting AUTH PLAIN
  received_emails = Queue.new
  smtp_auth_received = Queue.new
  smtp_server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0)
  smtp_port = smtp_server.addr[1]

  Thread.new do
    loop do
      client = smtp_server.accept
      Thread.new(client) do |sock|
        sock.puts "220 smtp.their-host.test ESMTP"
        in_data = false
        buf = +""
        while (line = sock.gets)
          if in_data
            if line.chomp == "."
              in_data = false
              received_emails << buf.dup
              buf.clear
              sock.puts "250 2.0.0 OK"
            else
              buf << line
            end
          else
            case line
            when /\AEHLO/i
              sock.puts "250-smtp.their-host.test"
              sock.puts "250 AUTH PLAIN LOGIN"
            when /\AAUTH PLAIN\s*(\S*)/i
              creds = $1.empty? ? sock.gets.strip : $1
              smtp_auth_received << creds.unpack1("m")
              sock.puts "235 2.7.0 Authentication successful"
            when /\AMAIL FROM/i, /\ARCPT TO/i
              sock.puts "250 2.1.0 OK"
            when /\ADATA/i
              in_data = true
              sock.puts "354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>"
            when /\AQUIT/i
              sock.puts "221 Bye"
              break
            else
              sock.puts "250 OK"
            end
          end
        end
        sock.close rescue nil
      end
    end
  rescue IOError
  end

  # 2. Simulate fork developer filling in hostname, mail server, and secrets in config/deploy.yml
  vapid = WebPush.generate_key
  skb = `bin/rails secret`.strip

  Dir.mktmpdir do |tmpdir|
    deploy_yml = File.read("config/deploy.yml")
      .gsub("fizzy.example.com", "fizzy.their-host.test")
      .gsub("smtp.example.com", "127.0.0.1")
      .gsub("SMTP_PORT: 587", "SMTP_PORT: #{smtp_port}")

    custom_deploy = File.join(tmpdir, "deploy.yml")
    File.write(custom_deploy, deploy_yml)

    ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"] = skb
    ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"] = "mailer_user"
    ENV["SMTP_PASSWORD"] = "mailer_secret_pw"
    ENV["VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY"] = vapid.public_key
    ENV["VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY"] = vapid.private_key

    config = Kamal::Configuration.create_from(config_file: Pathname.new(custom_deploy))
    role = config.role("web")
    raise "Expected SSL enabled" unless role.proxy.ssl?
    raise "Expected host fizzy.their-host.test" unless role.proxy.hosts == ["fizzy.their-host.test"]
    raise "Expected volume fizzy_storage:/rails/storage" unless config.volume_args == ["--volume", "fizzy_storage:/rails/storage"]

    container_env = role.env.clear.merge(
      role.env.secret_keys.to_h { |k| [k, config.secrets[k]] }
    ).merge(
      "RAILS_ENV" => "production",
      "HTTP_PORT" => "18080",
      "TARGET_PORT" => "13000",
      "WEB_CONCURRENCY" => "1"
    )

    puts "✓ Kamal configuration validated: proxy=#{role.proxy.deploy_options.slice(:host, :tls).inspect}"

    boot_container = -> do
      pid = spawn(container_env, "./bin/docker-entrypoint", "./bin/thrust", "./bin/rails", "server", out: "/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log", err: "/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log")
      60.times do
        res = Net::HTTP.get_response(URI("http://127.0.0.1:18080/up")) rescue nil
        return pid if res && res.code == "200"
        sleep 0.5
      end
      puts File.read("/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log")
      raise "Container failed to pass /up healthcheck"
    end

    stop_container = ->(pid) do
      Process.kill("TERM", pid)
      Process.wait(pid)
    end

    # 3. DEPLOY #1
    puts "=== Booting Deploy #1 ==="
    pid1 = boot_container.call
    puts "✓ Deploy #1 healthy on /up"

    # Trigger signup magic link via HTTP (as forwarded by kamal-proxy)
    http = Net::HTTP.new("127.0.0.1", 18080)
    headers = { "Host" => "fizzy.their-host.test", "X-Forwarded-Proto" => "https" }

    # Create an account + magic link + board + card + attachment, and enqueue MagicLinkMailer via Solid Queue
    runner_env = container_env
    system(runner_env, "bin/rails", "runner", <<~RUBY, exception: true)
      identity = Identity.create!(email_address: "alice@their-host.test")
      account = Account.create_with_owner(
        account: { name: "Acme Corp" },
        owner: { name: "Alice", identity: identity }
      )
      Current.account = account
      user = identity.users.find_by!(account: account)
      board = Board.create!(name: "Engineering", creator: user, all_access: true)
      card = board.cards.create!(title: "Deploy Fizzy on one box", creator: user, status: :published)
      card.image.attach(
        io: File.open(Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/avatar.png")),
        filename: "avatar.png",
        content_type: "image/png"
      )
      magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identity)
      MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link).deliver_later
    RUBY

    # Wait up to 10s for Solid Queue inside Puma to process MailDeliveryJob and deliver to mock SMTP!
    raw_email = Timeout.timeout(15) { received_emails.pop }
    auth_str = Timeout.timeout(5) { smtp_auth_received.pop }

    raise "Unexpected SMTP auth: #{auth_str.inspect}" unless auth_str == "\x00mailer_user\x00mailer_secret_pw"
    raise "Expected From header in email, got:\n#{raw_email}" unless raw_email.include?("Fizzy <noreply@fizzy.their-host.test>")
    raise "Expected https://fizzy.their-host.test passkey URL in email, got:\n#{raw_email}" unless raw_email.include?("https://fizzy.their-host.test/")
    puts "✓ Background job (Solid Queue in Puma) delivered magic link email via authenticated SMTP with https://fizzy.their-host.test URLs!"

    stop_container.call(pid1)
    puts "✓ Deploy #1 stopped cleanly"

    # 4. DEPLOY #2
    puts "=== Booting Deploy #2 (testing persistence across deploys) ==="
    pid2 = boot_container.call
    puts "✓ Deploy #2 healthy on /up after db:prepare"

    verify_out = IO.popen([runner_env, "bin/rails", "runner", <<~RUBY], &:read)
      account = Account.find_by!(name: "Acme Corp")
      Current.account = account
      card = Card.find_by!(title: "Deploy Fizzy on one box")
      raise "Image attachment missing!" unless card.image.attached? && card.image.download.bytesize > 0
      puts "SURVIVED: account=#{account.name} slug=#{account.slug} card=#{card.title} blob_bytes=#{card.image.download.bytesize}"
    RUBY
    raise "Verification failed: #{verify_out}" unless verify_out.include?("SURVIVED: account=Acme Corp")
    puts "✓ #{verify_out.lines.grep(/SURVIVED/).first.strip}"

    stop_container.call(pid2)
    puts "✓ Deploy #2 stopped cleanly"
  end
'

steps.message: Let's clean up any background process from the previous run and re-run the full end-to-end simulation (with `Current.with(account: account, user: user)` AND real HTTP requests through Thruster)!
steps.reasoning_content:
**Debugging a Testing Scenario**

Okay, so I've pinpointed the issue in our test script. It looks like when we're creating a `Card`, the `Current.user` isn't being properly initialized through `Current.with(account: account, user: user)`. This is problematic because the `Card` creation triggers an `Event` creation, and that `Event` is defaulting to `Current.user` as the `creator`. So, we're getting a null value there, which is causing failures.

Right, before we run the test, let's make sure we're killing any lingering `thrust` processes – `pkill -f thrust` should do the trick. Then, let's explicitly use `Current.with(account: account, user: user)` to set the current context for the test.

But wait, there's more. To really test this properly, let's go the extra mile! Instead of a basic integration test, let's have the test make REAL HTTP requests through Thruster to `https://fizzy.their-host.test`. This will give us a much more comprehensive view of the signup controller flow and make sure we're covering all our bases.

Right. Let's get this run running and see what happens!

arguments.command:
pkill -f "18080|13000|bin/thrust" 2>/dev/null || true
sleep 1
rm -rf storage/production* storage/thruster /tmp/e2e_fizzy.log

bundle exec ruby -rkamal -rsocket -rnet/http -rjson -rtimeout -rweb-push -e '
  # 1. Start a local mock SMTP server supporting AUTH PLAIN
  received_emails = Queue.new
  smtp_auth_received = Queue.new
  smtp_server = TCPServer.new("127.0.0.1", 0)
  smtp_port = smtp_server.addr[1]

  Thread.new do
    loop do
      client = smtp_server.accept
      Thread.new(client) do |sock|
        sock.puts "220 smtp.their-host.test ESMTP"
        in_data = false
        buf = +""
        while (line = sock.gets)
          if in_data
            if line.chomp == "."
              in_data = false
              received_emails << buf.dup
              buf.clear
              sock.puts "250 2.0.0 OK"
            else
              buf << line
            end
          else
            case line
            when /\AEHLO/i
              sock.puts "250-smtp.their-host.test"
              sock.puts "250 AUTH PLAIN LOGIN"
            when /\AAUTH PLAIN\s*(\S*)/i
              creds = $1.empty? ? sock.gets.strip : $1
              smtp_auth_received << creds.unpack1("m")
              sock.puts "235 2.7.0 Authentication successful"
            when /\AMAIL FROM/i, /\ARCPT TO/i
              sock.puts "250 2.1.0 OK"
            when /\ADATA/i
              in_data = true
              sock.puts "354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>"
            when /\AQUIT/i
              sock.puts "221 Bye"
              break
            else
              sock.puts "250 OK"
            end
          end
        end
        sock.close rescue nil
      end
    end
  rescue IOError
  end

  # 2. Simulate fork developer filling in hostname, mail server, and secrets in config/deploy.yml
  vapid = WebPush.generate_key
  skb = `bin/rails secret`.strip

  Dir.mktmpdir do |tmpdir|
    deploy_yml = File.read("config/deploy.yml")
      .gsub("fizzy.example.com", "fizzy.their-host.test")
      .gsub("smtp.example.com", "127.0.0.1")
      .gsub("SMTP_PORT: 587", "SMTP_PORT: #{smtp_port}")

    custom_deploy = File.join(tmpdir, "deploy.yml")
    File.write(custom_deploy, deploy_yml)

    ENV["SECRET_KEY_BASE"] = skb
    ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"] = "mailer_user"
    ENV["SMTP_PASSWORD"] = "mailer_secret_pw"
    ENV["VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY"] = vapid.public_key
    ENV["VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY"] = vapid.private_key

    config = Kamal::Configuration.create_from(config_file: Pathname.new(custom_deploy))
    role = config.role("web")
    raise "Expected SSL enabled" unless role.proxy.ssl?
    raise "Expected host fizzy.their-host.test" unless role.proxy.hosts == ["fizzy.their-host.test"]
    raise "Expected volume fizzy_storage:/rails/storage" unless config.volume_args == ["--volume", "fizzy_storage:/rails/storage"]

    role_env = role.env("fizzy.their-host.test")
    container_env = role_env.clear.transform_values(&:to_s).merge(
      role_env.secret_keys.to_h { |k| [k, config.secrets[k].to_s] }
    ).merge(
      "RAILS_ENV" => "production",
      "HTTP_PORT" => "18080",
      "TARGET_PORT" => "13000",
      "WEB_CONCURRENCY" => "1"
    )

    puts "✓ Kamal configuration validated: proxy=#{role.proxy.deploy_options.slice(:host, :tls).inspect}"

    boot_container = -> do
      pid = spawn(container_env, "./bin/docker-entrypoint", "./bin/thrust", "./bin/rails", "server", out: "/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log", err: "/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log")
      60.times do
        res = Net::HTTP.get_response(URI("http://127.0.0.1:18080/up")) rescue nil
        return pid if res && res.code == "200"
        sleep 0.5
      end
      puts File.read("/tmp/e2e_fizzy.log")
      raise "Container failed to pass /up healthcheck"
    end

    stop_container = ->(pid) do
      Process.kill("TERM", pid) rescue nil
      Process.wait(pid) rescue nil
    end

    pid1 = nil
    pid2 = nil
    begin
      # 3. DEPLOY #1
      puts "=== Booting Deploy #1 ==="
      pid1 = boot_container.call
      puts "✓ Deploy #1 healthy on /up"

      # Verify HTTP redirect via proxy headers preserves https://fizzy.their-host.test
      http = Net::HTTP.new("127.0.0.1", 18080)
      req = Net::HTTP::Get.new("/")
      req["Host"] = "fizzy.their-host.test"
      req["X-Forwarded-Proto"] = "https"
      res = http.request(req)
      raise "Expected redirect to https://fizzy.their-host.test/..., got #{res.code} #{res["location"]}" unless res.code == "302" && res["location"].start_with?("https://fizzy.their-host.test/")
      puts "✓ Proxy HTTPS request to / redirects to #{res["location"]}"

      # Create an account + magic link + board + card + attachment, and enqueue MagicLinkMailer via Solid Queue
      system(container_env, "bin/rails", "runner", <<~RUBY, exception: true)
        identity = Identity.create!(email_address: "alice@their-host.test")
        account = Account.create_with_owner(
          account: { name: "Acme Corp" },
          owner: { name: "Alice", identity: identity }
        )
        user = identity.users.find_by!(account: account)
        Current.with(account: account, user: user) do
          board = Board.create!(name: "Engineering", creator: user, all_access: true)
          card = board.cards.create!(title: "Deploy Fizzy on one box", creator: user, status: :published)
          card.image.attach(
            io: File.open(Rails.root.join("test/fixtures/files/avatar.png")),
            filename: "avatar.png",
            content_type: "image/png"
          )
        end
        magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identity)
        MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link).deliver_later
      RUBY

      # Wait up to 15s for Solid Queue inside Puma to process MailDeliveryJob and deliver to mock SMTP!
      raw_email = Timeout.timeout(15) { received_emails.pop }
      auth_str = Timeout.timeout(5) { smtp_auth_received.pop }

      raise "Unexpected SMTP auth: #{auth_str.inspect}" unless auth_str == "\x00mailer_user\x00mailer_secret_pw"
      raise "Expected From header in email, got:\n#{raw_email}" unless raw_email.include?("Fizzy <noreply@fizzy.their-host.test>")
      raise "Expected https://fizzy.their-host.test passkey URL in email, got:\n#{raw_email}" unless raw_email.include?("https://fizzy.their-host.test/")
      puts "✓ Background job (Solid Queue in Puma) delivered magic link email via authenticated SMTP with https://fizzy.their-host.test URLs!"

      stop_container.call(pid1)
      pid1 = nil
      puts "✓ Deploy #1 stopped cleanly"

      # 4. DEPLOY #2
      puts "=== Booting Deploy #2 (testing persistence across deploys) ==="
      pid2 = boot_container.call
      puts "✓ Deploy #2 healthy on /up after db:prepare"

      verify_out = IO.popen([container_env, "bin/rails", "runner", <<~RUBY], &:read)
        account = Account.find_by!(name: "Acme Corp")
        Current.account = account
        card = Card.find_by!(title: "Deploy Fizzy on one box")
        raise "Image attachment missing!" unless card.image.attached? && card.image.download.bytesize > 0
        raise "FTS5 search missing!" unless Search::Record.for(account.id).search("Deploy", user: account.users.first).any?
        puts "SURVIVED: account=#{account.name} slug=#{account.slug} card=#{card.title} blob_bytes=#{card.image.download.bytesize}"
      RUBY
      raise "Verification failed: #{verify_out}" unless verify_out.include?("SURVIVED: account=Acme Corp")
      puts "✓ #{verify_out.lines.grep(/SURVIVED/).first.strip}"

      stop_container.call(pid2)
      pid2 = nil
      puts "✓ Deploy #2 stopped cleanly"
    ensure
      stop_container.call(pid1) if pid1
      stop_container.call(pid2) if pid2
    end
  end
' && rm -rf storage/production* storage/thruster /tmp/e2e_fizzy.log

steps.reasoning_content:
**Aha! The Ruby Interpolation Bug!**

Okay, wait a minute... Line 168... *there* it is! That's it! I knew something was off! I see it now: `<<~RUBY` is interpolating `#{account.name}` in the *outer* Ruby script, but it shouldn't be. It needs to be `<<~'RUBY'` to prevent that interpolation and treat the string literally! I should have caught that earlier.

And the context... that's the best part. Look at all the stuff that *already* succeeded *before* that line was even reached! The Kamal configuration validated, the first deploy was healthy, the proxy redirection worked flawlessly, the background job sent the email with the correct URL... even a clean stop! And then the second deploy, healthy after db:prepare!

This is classic. All the clues are there. This rogue interpolation on line 168 is likely the only thing that could have gone wrong given all that evidence.

Changing that inner heredoc should make the entire test pass! Deploy #1 + Deploy #2, the whole shebang, will be perfect! Let's get that fixed and see everything validate from start to finish. I'm willing to bet this is the problem.

            if line.chomp == "."
              in_data = false
              received_emails << buf.dup
              buf.clear
              sock.puts "250 2.0.0 OK"
            else
              buf << line
            end
          else
            case line
            when /\AEHLO/i
              sock.puts "250-smtp.their-host.test"
              sock.puts "250 AUTH PLAIN LOGIN"
            when /\AAUTH PLAIN\s*(\S*)/i
              creds = $1.empty? ? sock.gets.strip : $1
              smtp_auth_received << creds.unpack1("m")
              sock.puts "235 2.7.0 Authentication successful"
            when /\AMAIL FROM/i, /\ARCPT TO/i
              sock.puts "250 2.1.0 OK"
            when /\ADATA/i

              sock.puts "354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>"
            when /\AQUIT/i
              sock.puts "221 Bye"
              break
            else
              sock.puts "250 OK"
            end
          end
        end
        sock.close rescue nil
      end
    end
  rescue IOError
  end

  skb = `bin/rails secret`.strip

      .gsub("smtp.example.com", "127.0.0.1")

          )
        end
        magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identity)
        MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link).deliver_later
      RUBY

      stop_container.call(pid1)
      pid1 = nil
      puts "✓ Deploy #1 stopped cleanly"

      # 4. DEPLOY #2
      puts "=== Booting Deploy #2 (testing persistence across deploys) ==="
      pid2 = boot_container.call
      puts "✓ Deploy #2 healthy on /up after db:prepare"

      verify_out = IO.popen([container_env, "bin/rails", "runner", <<~'\''RUBY'\''], &:read)
        account = Account.find_by!(name: "Acme Corp")
        Current.account = account
        card = Card.find_by!(title: "Deploy Fizzy on one box")
        raise "Image attachment missing!" unless card.image.attached? && card.image.download.bytesize > 0
        raise "FTS5 search missing!" unless Search::Record.for(account.id).search("Deploy", user: account.users.first).any?
        puts "SURVIVED: account=#{account.name} slug=#{account.slug} card=#{card.title} blob_bytes=#{card.image.download.bytesize}"
      RUBY
      raise "Verification failed: #{verify_out}" unless verify_out.include?("SURVIVED: account=Acme Corp")
      puts "✓ #{verify_out.lines.grep(/SURVIVED/).first.strip}"

      stop_container.call(pid2)
      pid2 = nil
      puts "✓ Deploy #2 stopped cleanly"
    ensure
      stop_container.call(pid1) if pid1
      stop_container.call(pid2) if pid2
    end
  end
' && rm -rf storage/production* storage/thruster /tmp/e2e_fizzy.log

steps.message: Let's test evaluating `config/environments/production.rb` against an isolated fake `Rails.application` in Minitest so we can test all `APP_HOST` and `SMTP_*` edge cases in milliseconds without touching global test state!
steps.reasoning_content:
**Testing the Kamal Deployment and Rails Configuration**

Okay, so I'm seeing that Kamal is included in both `Gemfile` and `Gemfile.saas` through an `eval_gemfile` call, and the `require: false` for the `kamal` gem in `Gemfile` means we explicitly require it in any test using `Kamal::Configuration`. Got it.

Now, I'm thinking about how to test the deployment configuration (`config/deploy.yml`), secrets file (`.kamal/secrets`), production environment (`config/environments/production.rb`), and the mailer (`ApplicationMailer`) efficiently and cleanly. Milliseconds, ideally, without the overhead of subprocesses.

I've got a plan. Two focused tests should do the trick:

1.  **`KamalDeployConfigTest`**: This will load and test the `config/deploy.yml` file via `Kamal::Configuration.create_from`, which includes validation and secrets parsing. It will assert:
    *   A single-container setup (one role, no accessories).
    *   SSL configuration from the proxy.
    *   Data persistence across deploys (volume args, asset path).
    *   Background jobs run on the box within the container.
    *   Correct hostname, mail server, and secrets being wired up by validating the correct env vars are set.

2.  **Mailer and Production Environment Tests**: I'll test `ApplicationMailer` and `config/environments/production.rb`. In a mailer test, I'll check that the `from` address is set properly, both the default and the custom `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS` from the environment.

    Now, regarding `config/environments/production.rb`, here's the clever bit: We need to test it without altering the running Rails application. The file starts with `Rails.application.configure do`. What if we can stub this?

    I'm thinking, instead of introducing abstractions, which would be against the `STYLE.md` guidelines, we can create a fake application object that mimics the required structure of the standard Rails app (with `config` and `routes` attributes). This object can have its `configure` method stubbed to `yields`. Then, by calling `fake_app.instance_eval` on the captured block (from `config/environments/production.rb`), we'll evaluate the file's configuration against the fake app in under a millisecond. This should work because `instance_eval` evaluates the block within the context of the fake app object. The file uses `config` and `routes`, and we can stub these onto our fake app.

    I need to check this idea, and the best way is to try it using `bin/rails runner` right now, so I'll check `Rails.stubs(:application)` with this lightweight fake app object to test evaluating `load Rails.root.join("config/environments/production.rb")` to see if it works as anticipated.

arguments.command:
bin/rails runner '
  require "mocha/minitest"
  fake_app = Class.new do
    attr_reader :config, :routes
    def initialize
      @config = Rails::Application::Configuration.new(Rails.root)
      @config.solid_queue = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
      @routes = Struct.new(:default_url_options).new({})
    end
    def configure(&block)
      instance_eval(&block)
    end
  end.new

  Rails.stubs(:application).returns(fake_app)
  ENV["APP_HOST"] = "fizzy.their-host.com"
  ENV["SMTP_ADDRESS"] = "smtp.their-host.com"
  ENV["SMTP_PORT"] = "465"
  ENV["SMTP_USERNAME"] = "u"
  ENV["SMTP_PASSWORD"] = "p"
  load Rails.root.join("config/environments/production.rb")

  p fake_app.routes.default_url_options
  p fake_app.config.action_controller.default_url_options
  p fake_app.config.action_mailer.default_url_options
  p fake_app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings
'

arguments.command:
cat <<'EOF' > test/lib/kamal_deploy_config_test.rb
require "test_helper"
require "kamal"

class KamalDeployConfigTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  test "default config/deploy.yml is valid for a single-box SSL SQLite deployment" do
    with_env(
      "SECRET_KEY_BASE" => "test-secret-key-base",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "smtp-user",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => "smtp-pass",
      "VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY" => "vapid-pub",
      "VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY" => "vapid-priv"
    ) do
      config = Kamal::Configuration.create_from(config_file: Rails.root.join("config/deploy.yml"))
      web_role = config.role("web")
      role_env = web_role.env(web_role.primary_host)

      assert_equal "fizzy", config.service
      assert_equal [ "web" ], config.roles.map(&:name)
      assert_empty config.accessories

      assert web_role.proxy.ssl?
      assert_equal 80, web_role.proxy.app_port
      assert_equal({ host: [ "fizzy.example.com" ], tls: true }, web_role.proxy.deploy_options.slice(:host, :tls))

      assert_includes config.volume_args, "fizzy_storage:/rails/storage"
      assert_equal "/rails/public/assets", config.raw_config.asset_path

      assert_equal true, role_env.clear["SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA"]
      assert_equal 1, role_env.clear["JOB_CONCURRENCY"]
      assert_equal "fizzy.example.com", role_env.clear["APP_HOST"]
      assert_equal "smtp.example.com", role_env.clear["SMTP_ADDRESS"]
      assert_equal 587, role_env.clear["SMTP_PORT"]

      assert_equal "test-secret-key-base", config.secrets["SECRET_KEY_BASE"]
      assert_equal "smtp-user", config.secrets["SMTP_USERNAME"]
      assert_equal "smtp-pass", config.secrets["SMTP_PASSWORD"]
      assert_equal "vapid-pub", config.secrets["VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY"]
      assert_equal "vapid-priv", config.secrets["VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY"]
    end
  end

  test "production environment configures URL options and STARTTLS SMTP from ENV" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => "https://fizzy.their-host.com/",
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => "smtp.their-host.com",
      "SMTP_PORT" => "587",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "mailer",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => "secret"
    )

    expected_url_options = { host: "fizzy.their-host.com", protocol: "https" }
    assert_equal expected_url_options, app.routes.default_url_options
    assert_equal expected_url_options, app.config.action_controller.default_url_options
    assert_equal expected_url_options, app.config.action_mailer.default_url_options

    assert_equal(
      {
        address: "smtp.their-host.com",
        port: 587,
        domain: "fizzy.their-host.com",
        user_name: "mailer",
        password: "secret",
        enable_starttls_auto: true
      },
      app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings
    )
  end

  test "production environment enables implicit TLS on port 465 without conflicting with STARTTLS" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => "fizzy.their-host.com",
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => "smtp.their-host.com",
      "SMTP_PORT" => "465",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "mailer",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => "secret"
    )

    smtp_settings = app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings
    assert_equal true, smtp_settings[:tls]
    assert_not smtp_settings.key?(:enable_starttls_auto)
    assert_nothing_raised { Mail::SMTP.new(smtp_settings).send(:build_smtp_session) }
  end

  test "production environment omits blank SMTP credentials and respects DISABLE_SSL" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => "fizzy.internal:3000",
      "DISABLE_SSL" => "true",
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => "relay.internal",
      "SMTP_PORT" => "25",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => ""
    )

    assert_equal({ host: "fizzy.internal:3000", protocol: "http" }, app.routes.default_url_options)
    assert_not app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings.key?(:user_name)
    assert_not app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings.key?(:password)
  end

  private
    def evaluate_production_config(env)
      fake_app = Struct.new(:config, :routes) do
        def configure(&block)
          instance_eval(&block)
        end
      end.new(
        Rails::Application::Configuration.new(Rails.root).tap do |c|
          c.active_storage = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.solid_queue = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.action_mailer = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.action_controller = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.i18n = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.active_support = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.active_record = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
        end,
        Struct.new(:default_url_options).new({})
      )

      with_env(env) do
        Rails.stubs(:application).returns(fake_app)
        load Rails.root.join("config/environments/production.rb")
      end

      fake_app
    end

    def with_env(vars)
      originals = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    end
end
EOF

require "test_helper"

class MagicLinkMailerTest < ActionMailer::TestCase
  test "sign_in_instructions" do
    magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identities(:kevin))
    email = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link)

    assert_emails 1 do
      email.deliver_now
    end

    assert_equal [ "kevin@37signals.com" ], email.to
    assert_equal [ "support@fizzy.do" ], email.from
    assert_equal "Your Fizzy code is #{ magic_link.code }", email.subject
    assert_match magic_link.code, email.body.encoded
  end

  test "uses MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS when configured" do
    old_from = ENV["MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS"]
    ENV["MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS"] = "Fizzy <noreply@their-host.example>"

    magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identities(:kevin))
    email = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link)

    assert_equal [ "noreply@their-host.example" ], email.from
  ensure
    ENV["MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS"] = old_from
  end
end

## Deploying Fizzy with Kamal

Fizzy ships with a single-server [Kamal](https://kamal-deploy.org) configuration in [`config/deploy.yml`](../config/deploy.yml). Everything runs in one container on one Linux box:

- **Web & assets**: Puma fronted by Thruster behind `kamal-proxy` with automatic Let's Encrypt SSL
- **Database, cache, cable, and job queue**: SQLite stored in a persistent Docker volume (`fizzy_storage:/rails/storage`)
- **File uploads & exports**: Active Storage on local disk inside `/rails/storage`
- **Background jobs**: Solid Queue running inside Puma (`SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA=true`)

### Prerequisites

1. A Linux server (`amd64` or `arm64`) with root SSH access and ports `80` and `443` open. (Kamal will install Docker automatically if needed.)
2. A DNS `A` / `AAAA` record pointing your hostname (for example, `fizzy.example.com`) at your server's IP address.
3. An outbound SMTP server so Fizzy can send sign-in codes and notifications.
4. Docker installed locally on the machine you deploy from.

### 1. Configure your hostname and mail server

    assert_equal expected_url_options, app.config.action_mailer.default_url_options

    assert_equal(
      {
        address: "smtp.their-host.com",
        port: 587,
        domain: "fizzy.their-host.com",
        user_name: "mailer",
        password: "secret",
        enable_starttls_auto: true
      },
      app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings
    )
  end

  test "production environment enables implicit TLS on port 465 without conflicting with STARTTLS" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => "fizzy.their-host.com",
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => "smtp.their-host.com",
      "SMTP_PORT" => "465",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "mailer",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => "secret"
    )

    smtp_settings = app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings
    assert_equal true, smtp_settings[:tls]
    assert_not smtp_settings.key?(:enable_starttls_auto)
    assert_nothing_raised { Mail::SMTP.new(smtp_settings).send(:build_smtp_session) }
  end

  test "production environment omits blank SMTP credentials and respects DISABLE_SSL" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => "fizzy.internal:3000",
      "DISABLE_SSL" => "true",
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => "relay.internal",
      "SMTP_PORT" => "25",
      "SMTP_USERNAME" => "",
      "SMTP_PASSWORD" => ""
    )

    assert_equal({ host: "fizzy.internal:3000", protocol: "http" }, app.routes.default_url_options)
    assert_not app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings.key?(:user_name)
    assert_not app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings.key?(:password)
  end

  test "production environment leaves preconfigured URL and SMTP settings untouched when ENV vars are unset" do
    app = evaluate_production_config(
      "APP_HOST" => nil,
      "SMTP_ADDRESS" => nil
    ) do |c|
      c.action_controller.default_url_options = { host: "app.fizzy.do", protocol: "https" }
      c.action_mailer.default_url_options = { host: "app.fizzy.do", protocol: "https" }
      c.action_mailer.smtp_settings = { address: "smtp-outbound", port: 25 }
    end

    assert_equal({ host: "app.fizzy.do", protocol: "https" }, app.config.action_controller.default_url_options)
    assert_equal({ host: "app.fizzy.do", protocol: "https" }, app.config.action_mailer.default_url_options)
    assert_equal({ address: "smtp-outbound", port: 25 }, app.config.action_mailer.smtp_settings)
  end

  private
    def evaluate_production_config(env, &preconfigure)
      fake_app = Struct.new(:config, :routes) do
        def configure(&block)
          instance_eval(&block)
        end
      end.new(
        Rails::Application::Configuration.new(Rails.root).tap do |c|
          c.active_storage = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.solid_queue = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.action_mailer = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.action_controller = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.i18n = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.active_support = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          c.active_record = ActiveSupport::OrderedOptions.new
          preconfigure&.call(c)
        end,
        Struct.new(:default_url_options).new({})
      )

      with_env(env) do
        Rails.stubs(:application).returns(fake_app)
        load Rails.root.join("config/environments/production.rb")
      end

      fake_app
    end

    def with_env(vars)
      originals = vars.keys.index_with { |key| ENV[key] }
      vars.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
      yield
    ensure
      originals.each { |key, value| ENV[key] = value }
    end
end

steps.message:
I have added a single-server Kamal deployment configuration and wired up production hostname and SMTP mail configuration so developers forking Fizzy can fill in their hostname, mail server, and secrets, run `kamal setup` (or `bin/kamal setup`), and run Fizzy at `https://their-host` in a single container with persistent SQLite storage and background jobs.

### Summary of Changes

- **Kamal configuration (`config/deploy.yml`, `.kamal/secrets`, `.dockerignore`)**:
  - Configured a single `web` container role (no separate job containers or external DB/Redis accessories) using Kamal's built-in local registry (`localhost:5555`) by default so no external container registry account is required.
  - Enabled automatic Let's Encrypt TLS via `kamal-proxy` (`proxy.ssl: true`, `proxy.host`).
  - Mounted a persistent Docker volume (`fizzy_storage:/rails/storage`) so all SQLite databases (`production`, `production_queue`, `production_cache`, `production_cable`) and local Active Storage uploads/exports survive across deploys, along with `asset_path: /rails/public/assets` for zero-downtime asset bridging.
  - Enabled Solid Queue inside Puma (`SOLID_QUEUE_IN_PUMA: true`, `JOB_CONCURRENCY: 1`) so background jobs run in the same container on the box.
  - Configured `APP_HOST`, `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_ADDRESS`, and `SMTP_PORT` in `env.clear`, and `SECRET_KEY_BASE`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY`, and `VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY` in `env.secret` / `.kamal/secrets`.
  - Excluded `/config/deploy*.yml` and `/.kamal` in `.dockerignore`.
- **Production URL & SMTP configuration (`config/environments/production.rb`, `app/mailers/application_mailer.rb`)**:
  - Configured `routes.default_url_options`, `config.action_controller.default_url_options`, and `config.action_mailer.default_url_options` from `APP_HOST` when set.
  - Configured `config.action_mailer.smtp_settings` from `SMTP_ADDRESS`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_DOMAIN`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`, `SMTP_AUTHENTICATION`, `SMTP_TLS` / `SMTP_SSL` (including automatic implicit TLS on port 465), `SMTP_ENABLE_STARTTLS_AUTO`, and `SMTP_OPENSSL_VERIFY_MODE`.
  - Updated `ApplicationMailer` default `from` to resolve `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS` dynamically with fallback to `Fizzy <support@fizzy.do>`.
- **Documentation & Tests (`docs/deployment.md`, `README.md`, `test/lib/kamal_deploy_config_test.rb`, `test/mailers/magic_link_mailer_test.rb`)**:
  - Added a deployment guide (`docs/deployment.md`) linked from `README.md`.
  - Added tests covering `config/deploy.yml`, `.kamal/secrets`, `MAILER_FROM_ADDRESS`, and production `APP_HOST` / `SMTP_*` settings.
